text:
zoe (support): heads up — ACME just opened SUP-2019, their prod p99 jumped to ~3.1s after last night's batcher tweak. p95 looks fine.
maria (oncall): ack. any idea which config changed? link or config id?
ashok (sre): config-service shows continuous-batcher/prod updated at 1750009000. changed hold_ms from 5 -> 25ms to squeeze throughput. suspect tiny-reqs are getting stuck.
kevin (runtime): ^ that change could make small-token requests wait for the window longer, esp when mixed with large KV warmups. need quick repro from their traffic pattern.
zoe (support): I grabbed a live repro using their key and a small prompt flood (avg 12 tokens). script below. reproduced p99 ~3s.
zoe (support): ```
for i in $(seq 1 300); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACME_KEY" \n    -d '{"model":"gpt-small","prompt":"hey","max_tokens":12}' &
  sleep 0.04
done
```
kevin (runtime): traces show a long wait in batch-coordinator: hold_time ~1.7s before flush for many requests. Also see KV-cache-miss spikes coincidentally.
ashok (sre): can you paste the live prod config? path: /configs/continuous-batcher/prod.yaml
zoe (support): prod snippet: ```
continuous_batcher:
  max_batch_size: 80
  hold_ms: 25
  grace_window_ms: 5
  smallreq_flush_tokens: 0   # disabled
  latency_priority: false
```
kevin (runtime): aha smallreq_flush_tokens==0 means no preferential flushing for small requests. quick mitigation: enable per-route smallreq flush and reduce hold_ms.
maria (oncall): customer is on dedicated lane and sensitive. prefer a route-scoped fix for ACME only. can we hotpatch?
kevin (runtime): yes — we can add an org override: routes.acme.continuous_batcher.smallreq_flush_tokens=24 and set hold_ms=10. will canary to their route first.
deploy-bot: initiating rollout: patch/continuous-batcher/hotfix-1750012345 -> canary(acme) at 1750012450
acme-monitoring-bot: alert: acme-prod p99=3120ms (5m window) baseline ~860ms
maria (oncall): monitoring: watch p95/p99, batch_wait hist, avg batch size, and gpu utilization. set alert for p99 > 1500ms during canary.
kevin (runtime): patch prepared: ```
continuous_batcher:
  max_batch_size: 80
  hold_ms: 10
  grace_window_ms: 5
  smallreq_flush_tokens: 24
  latency_priority: true
# route override
routes:
  org:acme:
    continuous_batcher:
      smallreq_flush_tokens: 24
      hold_ms: 10
```
kevin (runtime): note: still need to watch for decreased throughput / token cost impact. small batches may increase token/sec cost.
ashok (sre): I'll run a quick cost delta simulation on recent traffic slice.
zoe (support): canary update: after ~60s acme reports p99 down to ~940ms.
acme-monitoring-bot: update: acme-prod p99=940ms (2m window)
maria (oncall): looks better. keep canary for 15m then widen to 10% hosts.
kevin (runtime): also added a lightweight bypass: if request_tokens <= 8 then skip waiting on KV priming to avoid coupling tiny req latency to KV warmups.
ashok (sre): long-term: propose adaptive-hold where hold_ms scales with rolling token-size distribution per-route, plus explicit smallreq-flush as first-class config.
kevin (runtime): will open RFC for adaptive batching and route-level policies (ETA: EOD).
maria (oncall): action items: kevin -> hotfix PR + RFC; ashok -> cost impact check; zoe -> keep ticket open and confirm customer stable for 24h.
zoe (support): ACME is satisfied for now, staying on watch.
deploy-bot: rollout complete: patch/continuous-batcher/hotfix-1750012345 -> prod at 1750012601 :white_check_mark:
kevin (runtime): post-rollout checks look clean cluster-wide; schedule short postmortem note.
ashok (sre): created postmortem stub PM-ACME-BATCHER-HOLD-2026.
maria (oncall): closing thread for now, keep monitoring dashboards.
